decision: Escalate to the property manager. Two overlapping invoices (£138 and £372 inc VAT, same 5 Feb service date) are on file; invoice B claims actuator replacement that no authority covers and that no completion evidence, tenant sighting or file entry supports, and the contractor cannot reconcile them (event-022). Billing/liability and payment are outside my authority (PRO-PAYMENTS, PRO-TENANT-LIABILITY), and the underlying repair is still unresolved after nine days in a cold month with a child at the property (ESC-VULNERABLE). Within my mandate I reissued portable-heater safety advice and a status update to the tenant (ACT-1), chased the contractor with a 14 Feb 17:00 reply-by (ACT-2) and recorded the reconciliation note (ACT-3). I did not dispatch: the £372 remedial work is over the landlord's diagnosis-only £180 authority (APR-SPEND-OVER-CAP) and the landlord asked to be consulted first (event-005); current symptoms (partial/intermittent heating, hot water available, no smell, leak or warning) do not meet an emergency definition, so CAP-DISPATCH-EMERGENCY is not engaged.

facts.statement: Property is 7 Larkspur Fold, Orvane Heath, ZZ1 1ZZ; tenant Tessa Vane reported intermittent radiator heating on 3 Feb 2025 with hot water still available.
A child lives at the property; report made in February (cold month).
Tenant reported no visible leak, no unusual smell and no current warning light; access available after 14:00 on weekdays.
Landlord Soren Dallow authorised diagnosis only, up to £180 inc VAT, and asked to be consulted before any remedial work or further expenditure.

Copper Finch Mechanical quoted £138 inc VAT for attendance, diagnosis and testing and attended on 5 Feb 2025, reporting an intermittent heating valve actuator fault, no leak and no immediate gas-safety concern.

The landlord has not authorised the £372 work; on 6 Feb he asked whether the actuator could be repaired and whether the price covered all parts, labour and testing.
On 7 Feb the contractor said parts availability and estimate details still needed checking and confirmed no repair option, credit, return visit or completed actuator work.

Two invoices dated 10 Feb are on file for the same 5 Feb service date: A £138 inc VAT (attendance, diagnosis, inspection, operational test) and B £372 inc VAT (actuator supply and replacement, attendance, diagnosis, heating-system testing); descriptions overlap and neither states supersession.
The file contains no written authorisation for actuator replacement and no return-visit or completion entry.
On 10 Feb the tenant said she had seen no contractor since the 5 Feb visit, did not know whether the actuator was replaced, and that heating was working intermittently with one radiator cooler.

On 12 Feb the contractor said she was still checking and could not confirm whether the entries were separate chargeable work or whether one record replaced the other; no completion evidence, revised invoice or parts confirmation supplied.

Tenant is using one portable heater plugged directly into a wall socket, with no new smell, leak or warning reported.

options: Hold both invoices pending signed completion and parts evidence, pay nothing now, and ask the landlord to authorise a second heating engineer for a fresh fixed-price diagnosis and repair — slower on billing, fastest route to a working heating system.

Keep Copper Finch: require one corrected invoice (diagnosis credited against the replacement) plus job notes and parts record, and get the landlord to authorise the corrected figure before any return visit — cheapest if the evidence stands, but relies on a contractor who has twice failed to reconcile.

Treat the £372 as a billing irregularity: formal query to Copper Finch's principal, stand them down from this job, and instruct a replacement engineer with landlord approval — strongest control, loses the only engineer who has seen the fault.
